correctness.rationale: A root with r binary transitions yields 2r plus a possible central transition in its square. The five-run host has four transitions, giving the exhaustive unary, one-transition and two-transition root cases. Forced complete middle runs and the interval for the split center yield the exact set; disjointness follows from root run counts and orientations. Explicit inequalities prove the sharp total and mixed maxima for all positive parameters. A positive-parameter lattice-point decomposition proves the rational GFs; pole comparison and Dirichlet-simplex convergence give the distributional facts. Independent definition-based enumeration matched complete square sets for 3125 tuples and full finite-length histograms through 26; finite tests alone are not treated as proof.

value.rationale: This natural five-run string family has a complete count and explicit set for a central stringology invariant, not merely an isolated special case. It identifies the first run-count threshold for linearly many distinct mixed exact squares, proves all such mixed squares synchronize in length, attains two distinct sharp full-length extremal laws and quantifies a rare equality-of-interior-runs resonance by two exact rational generating functions and a probabilistic limit. These structural and enumerative results are not consequences of generic published upper bounds.
